source_anchors.operation: IMBegin is a lower_bound under MSSpectrum::IMLess, which compares getDriftTime(); only the const overload is declared even though the class test names a mutable one
IMEnd is the matching upper_bound
MSSpectrum::IMLess::operator() compares a.getDriftTime() < b.getDriftTime(), so the scalar drift time alone orders the scans

isIMFrame: empty run returns false; the first spectrum's RT is the reference, compared with !=; last_drift starts at numeric_limits<double>::lowest() and only the previous scan is compared, so a single scan with no drift time reports true

get2DPeakDataIMPerSpectrum declares DriftTimeUnit unit, std::vector<float> im and float t = -1.0 before the loop, so a first selected RT of exactly -1 opens no row and mz.back() writes into an empty vector

the row key is the f64 RT compared against the f32 cursor, and maybeGetIMData() is called only when a row starts, so spectra merged into one row are looked up in the first spectrum's ion mobility array
im[peak_index] with peak_index = it.getPeakIndex().peak, the peak's index inside its own spectrum, and no comparison against im.size()
a spectrum whose maybeGetIMData() reports DriftTimeUnit::NONE contributes the sentinel -1.0 per peak, the same value a genuine mobility of -1 would produce
get2DPeakDataIM declares unit, im and t = -1.0 INSIDE the per-peak loop, so the array is refetched per peak and a spectrum at RT exactly -1 reports -1 mobility although it carries ion mobility data
rasterizeRTMZ throws Exception::NullPointer for a null buffer and Exception::InvalidValue for a zero bin count, then Exception::InvalidRange for min >= max on either axis
total_pixels = rt_bins * mz_bins is computed unchecked and then filled through the caller's pointer

the single-threaded rasterizer branch this port reproduces: `if (num_threads <= 1)` at 355, rt_bin clamped to rt_bins-1, mz window from MZBegin/MZEnd, pixel index mz_bin * rt_bins + rt_bin, SUM or MAX, returning at 398

the single-threaded branch skips a whole spectrum when rt_bin < 0 (362) and one peak when mz_bin < 0 (the mz_bin >= 0 tests at 376 and 388); both are unreachable because RTBegin/MZBegin are lower_bound calls and min < max is enforced, so they can fire only on unsorted input, which this port rejects with Error::UnsortedData first

the OpenMP branch: per-thread f32 accumulation buffers allocated at 402-406, `#pragma omp parallel for` at 409 with the loop body to 487, the same negative-bin skips at 425-428 and 453/472, and the merge into the output at 489-517; the function ends at 518. The port is serial and records the gap

each thread adds into its own f32 buffer (460) and the merge then adds those partial sums into the pixel (499), so for RasterAggregation::SUM the f32 summation order and therefore the rounded result differ between the parallel and the single-threaded branch; for MAX they agree, because a maximum is associative and commutative
areaBegin(const RangeManagerType&, UInt) reads RangeRT, RangeMZ and RangeMobility with getNonEmptyRange() and ignores RangeIntensity
the scalar areaBegin passes RangeMobility{}.getNonEmptyRange(), a full range, so an unrestricted mobility filter is the source default
Param::lowIM / highIM store the mobility boundary; both default to lowest()/max()
AreaIterator::getDriftTime returns current_scan_->getDriftTime(), the scalar value, never a per-peak array
nextScan_ constructs RangeMobility mb {p_.low_im_, p_.high_im_} on every call, before the scan loop; RangeMobility inherits RangeBase's constructors (RangeManager.h:486)
nextScan_ skips a scan whose MS level differs or whose drift time is not contained in RangeMobility{low_im_, high_im_}; the level is compared after uint8_t/int8_t narrowing

RangeBase(min, max) throws Exception::InvalidRange when min > max (the check at 51), so a reversed lowIM/highIM pair makes AreaIterator::nextScan_ throw rather than silently select nothing; a NaN bound does not throw, because min_ > max_ is false for NaN
RangeBase::contains is min <= value & value <= max, which answers false for NaN, so a scan with a NaN drift time is silently skipped even by a full range
getNonEmptyRange returns (lowest, max) for an empty range, which is why an empty dimension of a RangeManager does not restrict the area
getIMUnit decides from the array NAME only: a PSI-MS child of MS:1002893 with its declared unit, then the UserParam prefixes; the array's own 'unit' meta value is never read
OPENMS_PRECONDITION expands to nothing unless OPENMS_ASSERTIONS is defined, so the areaBegin swapped-bound and isSorted guards do not exist in a release build
the exp_area fixture: set2DData of six RT/m/z points becomes three scans (RT -1, 1, 2) and drift times 0, 1, 2 are assigned afterwards

copy assignment (115-140, 7 macros) and move assignment (142-174, 9 macros): one contact named "Name" and one spectrum with peaks at m/z 5 and 10; the copy reports contacts size 1, size 1, getMinMZ 5.0 and getMaxMZ 10.0, assignment from a temporary empties both, and the moved-from container has size 0

the first updateRanges section (429-603, 64 macros): four scans with drift times 99, 99, 199, 66 give combined mobility 66..199 and MS1 m/z 5.0..7.0; the chromatogram block adds product m/z 80 and 100 and RT 0.1..0.3

getClosestSpectrumInRT(RT, ms_level) over RTs 30,31,32,40,41,50,60,61 at levels 1,2,2,1,2,1,1,2; line 829 asserts that ms_level 0 answers cend() because no scan carries that level, which the port does not reproduce because it reserves 0 as the any-level wildcard of the single-argument overload
the get2DPeakDataIMPerSpectrum fixture and its six cases, including the -1.0 sentinel for a spectrum with no ion mobility array

the second updateRanges section (2735-2915, 50 macros): four dual-range sub-cases plus a three-level tail; the mixed run reports combinedRanges().getMinMZ() == 0 because the chromatogram's Product m/z is unset, and chromatogramRanges().hasRange() == ALL
the backward-compatibility section: getMinMobility/getMaxMobility read the combined range manager, and the minimum m/z is 0 because the chromatogram's product m/z is unset
the getDriftTime section: lowIM(1).highIM(1.5) over RT [3,9] and m/z [503,509] keeps only the scan with drift time 1.4
the overall test's mobility cases: lowIM(0).highIM(2) selects all eight peaks, lowIM(0).highIM(0.9) selects none

evidence: Tier 3 (source review): every literal in tests/experiment_mobility.rs is transcribed from the two pinned class tests. No C++ was built or executed and no retained C++ output exists for these headers, so tier 1 is unavailable. Class-test section accounting across both files: 81 sections, 56 ported (a Rust test asserts the section's own literals), 21 mapped (no transcription, but a named Rust test function asserts a concrete value exercising the same member; every mapped section carries five assertion macros or fewer), 4 unaccounted. The per-section tables with the test function and the asserted value for each are in docs/EXPERIMENT_MOBILITY_SUPPORT.md. This replaces the previous claim of 14 ported and 63 mapped, which an audit found unsupported: the earlier revision of the support document accounted for 54 MSExperiment_test.cpp sections with a bare list of nine Rust test files and named no test function and no asserted value for any of them, and 22 of those 54 carried more than five assertion macros and therefore had to be ported, not mapped. The four unaccounted sections are the set2DData add_mass_traces specialization (10 macros), both getFirstProductSpectrum overloads (11 and 10) and operator<<(ostream&, const MSExperiment&) (5) - the three deferrals recorded in the support document, each needing a file outside this work package's ownership. Macro counts exclude TEST_PRECONDITION_VIOLATED, which OPENMS_PRECONDITION compiles away in a release build. Everything the port checks that the source does not - the drift-time ordering and finiteness guards, the ion mobility array length guard, the raster sortedness and finiteness guards, the resource ceilings and the atomic commit - is tier 4 (Rust-only invariants) derived from the source lines anchored above.
